speaker_role: current admissions officers (Skidmore College, UMass Lowell, University of Vermont, Merrimack College) plus a representative from Landmark College, which serves students with learning differences
commercial_incentive: none evident; school representatives promoting their own institutions as part of a general public panel
key_insights: Suggests starting list-building with local college visits, guidebooks, and institutional websites, noting schools invest heavily in accurate website content
A useful exercise: list schools by intended major first in a spreadsheet, then narrow by fit factors (public/private, size, specific communities like HBCUs)
Reach/target/safety categorization should be paired with financial fit; every school is legally required to post a net price calculator
A 'healthy' college list can range from roughly 5 to 15 schools with no fixed ideal number
Cited that only about 17% of students who received high school accommodations go on to access disability support resources in college, with worse degree-completion outcomes if they don't

Colleges offer a spectrum of disability/learning-difference support: baseline legally-required accommodations, added support services (coaching, labs), structured programs, and a small number of specialized colleges (e.g. Landmark, Beacon)
Student-to-faculty ratio is an average and doesn't reveal actual first-year class sizes; suggests asking specifically about first-year seminar caps and advising structure
specific_numbers_or_facts: 17% of students who received high school accommodations go on to access college disability resources (per Landmark College rep, citing National Center for Learning Disabilities)
Nationwide bachelor's completion rate cited as roughly 50%+, and about 33-34% for students with learning differences (per Landmark rep)
Skidmore's student-faculty ratio cited as 8:1; Landmark's cited as 6:1 with an 8-12 student average class size (per respective reps)
notable_or_distinctive: Includes a dedicated segment on choosing colleges based on disability/learning-difference support infrastructure, a topic covered with unusual specificity compared to generic list-building content.
reliability_notes: Recorded during 2020 amid COVID; testing-policy and enrollment-uncertainty details discussed are specific to that period and likely dated; otherwise first-person admissions officer claims.
